# ADR-1116: claude[bot] reviews run from main via workflow_run with staged gate activation

## Status

superseded by [ADR-1117](https://github.com/cdeust/Cortex/blob/main/wiki/adr/cortex/1117-use-the-official-anthropic-direct-pr-review-workflow.md), shipped in PR 807 as main commit 7a85eb38af278541aaf6507829e998e8e4d8e7e7. The workflow_run marker protocol described below is historical.

## Context

Owner direction 2026-10-27: restore genuine claude[bot] code and security reviews on every same-repository PR push, alongside the native Codex gate, without a pending hardlock. anthropics/claude-code-action v1.0.263 (8041f1d17e0e7d2f2cfe35002962e9f26237c0bb) exchanges a GitHub OIDC token for a claude[bot] App token at api.anthropic.com; the exchange refuses a workflow whose content differs from the default branch and the action then soft-skips green without posting (src/github/token.ts:24-54,129-136; src/entrypoints/run.ts:179-183). Passing github_token changes the identity to github-actions[bot], rejected by the owner. pull_request_review runs the workflow file from refs/pull/N/merge, so an Actions-write job under it is PR-controlled (repo invariant test_completion_workflow_never_checks_out_candidate_or_uses_oauth). The App token has contents:write and is revoked when the action step ends (action.yml:448). The Codex completion catch reruns a green waiting Pipeline whenever Codex is complete; without Claude in its proof it would loop while Claude is pending.

## Decision

1. .github/workflows/claude.yml reviews on workflow_run of Pipeline (types requested, run_attempt 1), so main's copy always runs and the OIDC exchange accepts it. Jobs: target (read-only, server-derived PR), review (Claude on a main checkout, PR read as a diff file, publishes a COMMENT review on commit_id=head with first line <!-- claude-review:v2 kind=code|security findings=N run=<run id>-<attempt> --> through one exact allowed Bash command, with --setting-sources user and --permission-mode dontAsk so repository settings grant nothing more; concurrency per head, never cancelled), verify (fresh runner, read-only reader), resume (only actions:write job, shares Codex.yml's concurrency group, calls the shared coordinator). No pull_request_review trigger. 2. Evidence = claude[bot] (type Bot) reviews on the exact head whose cited run attempt the Actions API shows is a claude.yml workflow_run on main with job `review <head>` whose `Validate <kind> review execution` step succeeded; that step validates the execution file and that this attempt published exactly its pre-created verdict file. Markers without such a producer (an @claude session, a manual post) are not evidence and do not suppress the CI review; a duplicate kind or malformed bound marker fails; findings>0 block until a new head; absent stays pending, never failed. 3. The shared coordinator proof combines Codex and Claude (scripts/ci_codex_review_resume.py combined_proof). 4. Activation is read from main's claude.yml line (scripts/ci_claude_review_gate.py; an unrecognised declaration fails loudly) `CLAUDE_REVIEW_GATE: required` via the contents API; observe or absent gives the distinct state not_required (Codex-only). The installing PR ships observe; a one-line follow-up PR flips it after a hosted claude[bot] review is observed.

## Consequences

Easier: a PR that edits CI is still reviewed by claude[bot]; a green Claude job is never treated as evidence; the installing PR cannot be blocked by its own gate; a defect found on the first hosted run cannot hardlock merges. Harder: inline @claude in review comments no longer triggers (issue_comment and issues only); once required, a broken review path on main keeps every PR truthfully pending until the secret or main workflow is fixed (owner rerun or admin merge of the fix); the @claude tag job, now limited to the repository owner with subprocess secret scrubbing, can still post as claude[bot]; it cannot create a validated claude.yml run, so its markers are ignored, and a marker citing a genuine attempt fails closed as a duplicate (docs/verification/claude-bot-ci-20261027.md).
